operating_notes.text: Step-down subsidiary PCJ Mining SARL obtained a one-year gold mining license in the Republic of Chad.
The company executed a Memorandum of Understanding with the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) to serve as an Industry/Franchise Partner for the Gems & Jewellery sector.
PCJ Mining SARL incorporated in the Republic of Chad and granted a license for semi-mechanized artisanal gold mining.
Q2FY27 raw material cost ₹630.30 Cr, down 20.5% YoY, against revenue of ₹1,054.47 Cr.
Received ₹142.14 Cr from export debtors in Q2FY27; AD banks approved ₹13.16 Cr of additional discounts to foreign buyers.
PCJ Mining SARL (66% held by PCJ Gems & Jewellery) commenced on-site development work on its Chad gold mining licence in Q2FY27.
Company achieved debt-free status after repaying all consortium bank dues.
Company successfully converted all 9,72,22,222 fully convertible warrants issued to promoter Shri Balram Garg, raising ₹131.25 crore.

timeline.summary: PC Jeweller's step-down subsidiary PCJ Mining SARL secured a one-year gold mining license in Chad.
PC Jeweller released monitoring agency reports for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, detailing the utilisation of preferential issue proceeds.
PC Jeweller reported standalone Q4 FY26 revenue of ₹927 Cr; with PAT at ₹150 Cr and progress on debt reduction.
Balram Garg (Promoter) and Pooja Garg/Balram Garg (HUF) confirmed no encumbrance on PC Jeweller shares during FY2026 under SEBI Reg. 31(4).
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,054.47 Cr (+27.8% YoY), net profit ₹330.66 Cr (+57.8% YoY).
PC Jeweller reported Q2FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹1,054 Cr and became debt-free after settling dues with all 14 banks.
PC Jeweller completed the conversion of all 9,72,22,222 fully convertible warrants, raising ₹131.25 Cr with no deviation in fund utilization.

status_history.evidence: AD banks approved additional discounts of ₹13.16 Cr to foreign buyers; company pursuing approvals for discounts on remaining outstanding bills.
